//: Provenance for the captured `claude --output-format stream-json` transcripts
beside this file. Data, not documentation — `.claude/rules/amberx-bound-builds.md`
§3 bans GizmoX-shaped docs for AmberX-bound work, and a fixture with no record of
how it was produced cannot be re-captured when the CLI changes.
These are REAL runs against the owner's subscription (CLI mode, no API key), taken
for axf-claude.bmpx P0: 'DESIGN AGAINST A CAPTURED TRANSCRIPT, NOT AN IMAGINED ONE.'

captures.intent: The broad one — every event kind a healthy agentic turn produces.
proves: text deltas and whole assistant messages (SEVEN of them in one turn — the tool loop that makes `text = whole` a truncating bug)
tool_use for 7 distinct tools with complete inputs (Write, Edit, Read, Bash, Agent, TaskCreate, TaskUpdate)
tool_result in both observed shapes: a bare string, and an array of content blocks
file edits as real Write/Edit tool inputs
todos — this environment exposes TaskCreate/TaskUpdate rather than TodoWrite; recorded as observed, not normalised into a todo concept that does not exist here
subagents: system/task_started, task_progress, task_updated, task_notification, and subagent traffic threaded by a non-null parent_tool_use_id
usage on message_delta and on the final result, including the cache-token spread (67 input vs 464,153 cache-read)
a successful terminal result (subtype 'success') carrying total_cost_usd

captures.intent: Went looking for a permission request. Found that there isn't one.
proves: --disallowed-tools REMOVES the tool from the session rather than denying its use: the model never asks, and permission_denials stays empty. Disallowed is not denied.
a long unbroken thinking run (29 thinking_delta events) — the fold-this-away case for a UI

captures.intent: The error path. One line long, and the most load-bearing fixture here.
proves: a failed turn is subtype 'error_during_execution' with is_error true
THERE IS NO `result` FIELD — the reason is only in `errors: [...]`. GizmoX's broker reads `r.result` for its error message and would have reported an empty string.
the process exits 1 and repeats the reason on stderr

captures.intent: The refusal channel that actually exists in headless mode.
proves: a permissions.deny rule surfaces as an ordinary tool_result with is_error true and a <tool_use_error> payload — that is what a UI renders red
permission_denials[] on the result stays empty for deny rules, so it is a post-hoc ledger and not the live channel

notCaptured.finding: Headless `-p` mode has no prompt-shaped permission event. Four captures went looking (b and e are the two kept). A UI built expecting one would wait for something this transport never sends; the renderable failure is the is_error tool_result in capture e.
notCaptured.wouldNeed: --input-format stream-json with a permission-prompt tool, i.e. the bidirectional control channel — out of scope for P0.
